definitions.gloss: Honganji, the head temple of Jōdo Shinshū
definitions.explanation: The head temple of Jōdo Shinshū Buddhism in Kyoto, which grew from Shinran's mausoleum. Since about 1602 it has been two temples, Nishi (West) Honganji and Higashi (East) Honganji, heading two branches of the school.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {西本願寺|にしほんがんじ} / {東本願寺|ひがしほんがんじ}: the two head temples in Kyoto
- お⟦{西|にし}→西：00659_nishi⟧さん / お⟦{東|ひがし}→東：02250_higashi⟧さん: the affectionate Kyoto names for them
- ⟦{築地|つきじ}→築地：31032_tsukiji⟧{本願寺|ほんがんじ}: the large branch temple in Tokyo

CULTURAL NOTE:
In the sixteenth century the Honganji was also a military power: its fortified temple at {石山|いしやま} in Osaka held out against ⟦{織田信長|おだのぶなが}→織田信長：30992_odanobunaga⟧ for ten years (1570–1580). The split into east and west followed under the Tokugawa.
